ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory PEP, OFAC, UN, and domestic screening standards (concise and factual): FINTRAC require whether a client is a politically exposed domestic or foreign person; screening of all ultimate beneficial owners against the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) sanctions lists and the Treasury Board of Canada SecretarInfo sanctioned persons; United Nations Security Council consolidated list; Canada's Special Economic Measures Regulations; United States OFAC sanctions screening mandatory for any cross-border USD transactions or US nexus; enhanced due diligence for high-risk jurisdictions and all 25%+ UBOs; transaction monitoring for Politically Exposed Foreign Persons (PEFPs) and domestic PEPs under FINTRAC guidelines.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be available under the Business Corporations Act (Alberta) and cannot be confusing with existing names or protected marks. The name must be composed of English or French words (or a combination) using Roman characters; Alberta does not permit Cyrillic, CJK, or Arabic script in the official corporate name, but transliteration into Roman characters is permitted for trade names. Suffix must be 'ULC' or 'Compagnie a responsabilite illimitee' for unlimited liability corporations.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: In case of name rejection, applicant has 30 days to file an administrative appeal with the Director of Corporate Registry under the Alberta Corporate Registry Regulation. The appeal must include a statement of eligibility, the submitted NUANS report, and the proposed articles. If administrative review is unsuccessful, judicial review may be sought under the Judicial Review Procedure Act, R.S.A. 2000, c. J-1, within the limitation period.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual offices are permitted in Alberta only if a physical street address is maintained in the province and is not a post office box. A commercial registered office service may serve as the physical registered office for low-risk OEM distribution; however, the corporation must hold its statutory records and minute book at that location or allow inspection at a reasonable alternative commercial location in Alberta.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: (Low - estimated 5% risk for a low-risk standard industry; no mandatory license required, so risk limited to unannounced registry compliance audits)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (Alberta), RSA 2000, c B-9, as amended (ABCA); ss 9-16 (incorporation and articles), ss 21-22 (registered office and records), ss 101-109 (share capital), s 21.1 (unlimited liability corporation designation), ss 173-174 (board of directors), and ss 211-220 (officers and unanimous shareholder agreements).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, Service Alberta, Government of Alberta
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form 1 Articles of Incorporation and Certificate of Incorporation
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital or escrow deposit is required for an Alberta unlimited liability corporation. The articles must specify authorized shares; issued share capital is credited as fully paid and non-assessable per the subscription agreement.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that the corporation accept the share subscription of the incorporator set forth in the subscription schedule, allot and issue the subscribed common shares as fully paid and non-assessable; RESOLVED that the registered head office and mailing address of the corporation be established at [Registered Office Address] in Alberta, Canada; RESOLVED further that [Name] be appointed President and [Name] be appointed Secretary-Treasurer, each to serve until the next annual general meeting or until successors are duly elected; and RESOLVED that the officers be authorized to open and maintain corporate bank accounts, execute banking resolutions, register for tax identification numbers, and file all statutory returns.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry (Service Alberta) online portal / authorized registry agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name search and reservation request through the Alberta Corporate Registry Online System; ensure a corporate name ending in 'ULC' or 'Unlimited Liability Corporation'; pay the name reservation fee; obtain the name reservation certificate valid for 90 days.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused for confusing similarity, file an amended name reservation or a revised name under the same application; any refusal may be reconsidered in writing within 15 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting of Articles of Incorporation and Statutory Consents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Applicant's legal counsel / registered Alberta agent for pre-filing review
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare Form 1 Articles of Incorporation, including the unlimited liability designation, authorized share structure, restrictions and director information; execute Form 2 Notice of Registered Office and director consent forms; finalize the share subscription schedule.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Revise and re-execute the affected schedules if the registry queries missing or inconsistent particulars; resubmit within the query response deadline.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upload the executed Form 1 and Form 2, attach the name reservation certificate and director consents; pay the state filing fee of CAD 500 (approx. USD 380); receive the Certificate of Incorporation upon approval.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is objected to, file corrective supplementary materials or amended Articles through the Corporate Registry's query process within 30 days; legal counsel may submit written submissions in support of the request.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Establishment of Registered Office and Corporate Records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registered office in Alberta / corporate records officer
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open the physical registered office in Alberta; install the corporate minute book, share register, seal and by-law records; maintain the statutory books at the registered head office as required by ABCA.
required_dossiers: Lease or ownership documents for the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If records are found incomplete during later compliance, remedy by preparing a corporate records restoration package and filing a Notice of Change if the registered office address changes.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Organizational Meeting and First Board Resolution
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Initial Board of Directors of the ULC
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the organizational board meeting; adopt the first board resolution approving share subscription, registered office, officers and banking authorities; file executed minutes and officer consents in the minute book.
required_dossiers: First board resolution and meeting minutes
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a physical meeting is not possible, pass all required resolutions unanimously in writing in lieu of a meeting under ABCA; no separate filing is required for internal resolutions.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency, Workers' Compensation Board – Alberta, and local municipal license service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the ULC for a federal Business Number, corporate income tax account, and GST/HST account through CRA Business Registration Online; register as an Alberta employer with WCB and obtain any municipal business or home-based business licence for the manufacturing address.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA rejects or queries the registration, resubmit with updated articles and incumbency certificate; deficiencies in provincial or municipal licences may be cured by completing the arrear notices and re-inspecting the premises.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Municipal business licensing department (e.g., City of Calgary or City of Edmonton Development and Business Licence Services) and Alberta Municipal Affairs
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No sector-specific statutory operating licence is mandated for plush toy OEM manufacturing; a general Municipal Business Licence and applicable development/building permit are required for physical operations.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – not designated under the Environmental Protection and Enhancement Act (EPEA) for a full Environmental Impact Assessment; registration or approval may apply if operating a waste storage or solvent-bearing process.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with Alberta Ambient Air Quality Objectives and EPEA release limits; wastewater discharges must meet municipal sewer bylaws (e.g., pH 6-9, no unpermitted priority pollutants); fabric dust and adhesive VOC levels must not exceed Alberta Occupational Exposure Limits and CCME cumulative effects thresholds; solid fabric waste handling must follow the Alberta Waste Control Regulation.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety inspection and certification under the Alberta Fire Code; structural load and life-safety review under the Alberta Building Code; occupational clearance obtained by registering with the Workers' Compensation Board – Alberta and complying with the Alberta Occupational Health and Safety Code for machine guarding, noise, and indoor air.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA), via the Business Registration Online (BRO) portal and GST/HST NETFILE system; Alberta provincial corporate tax is administered by CRA under a collection agreement with Alberta Finance. Portal: https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency.html and https://www.alberta.ca/corporate-tax.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign-owned Alberta ULC: (1) incorporate the ULC under the Alberta Business Corporations Act and receive a Corporate Access Number from Alberta Corporate Registry; (2) register with CRA through BRO to obtain a 9-digit federal Business Number (BN) and the associated GST/HST, corporate income tax (T2), payroll, and import/export programs; (3) complete the Alberta provincial corporate tax registration and appoint a local registered office and, if none resident, an Alberta agent for service; (4) obtain separate import/export identification if engaging in cross-border shipments; (5) provide non-resident ownership details and complete any FATCA/CRS documentation.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No Canadian 'check-the-box' election; a ULC is a resident Canadian corporation for domestic tax purposes. However, the entity is eligible for U.S. check-the-box treatment via IRS Form 8832, allowing it to be treated as a disregarded entity or partnership for U.S. tax purposes. Canada's hybrid mismatch rules (Income Tax Act ss. 17.1, 18.4, 94, 212.3) and the Canada-US treaty provisions may recharacterize certain hybrid arrangements. Alberta has no separate entity classification election.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (Goods and Services Tax/Harmonized Sales Tax); Alberta applies the federal 5% GST only and has no provincial sales tax.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory real-time electronic invoicing, fiscal clearance, or digital stamping is currently required by the CRA. CRA accepts electronic invoices, and GST/HST returns may be filed electronically through GST/HST NETFILE, EDI, or API integrations. Alberta imposes no separate provincial sales tax filing or clearance system.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under the Excise Tax Act (ETA), Schedule VI, a GST/HST registrant may zero-rate the supply of tangible personal property (the plush mascots) when the goods are supplied to a non-resident and delivered outside Canada for consumption outside Canada, or delivered by the registrant to a common carrier for export. For goods shipped under a normal export sale, the registrant must maintain proof that the goods were physically exported within a reasonable time (generally within 60 days, unless a longer period is reasonable), and if the purchaser exports the goods without the registrant shipping them, the conditions of Part V, Sections 5 or 6 of Schedule VI must be met. Offshore services directly related to exported goods may also be zero-rated.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: CBSA B13A Export Declaration (or Canadian Automated Export Declarations report number) for shipments subject to export reporting
Commercial invoice showing export sale, destination country, incoterms, and zero-rated tax status
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill evidencing physical transportation outside Canada
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank payment proof from the foreign buyer
GST/HST export evidence checklist and sales documentation supporting the export exemption
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA may reassess within 4 years of the reporting period, or indefinitely if misrepresentation or fraud is proven. Improper zero-rating claims are subject to the ETA s. 285.1 penalty of 50% of the incorrectly claimed tax refund or credit, plus compounding interest. Knowingly making false statements or evasion can trigger criminal prosecution, fines up to 200% of the tax evaded, and imprisonment. CRA may claw back any previously claimed input tax credits or refunds and reassess to charge GST/HST plus penalties and arrears interest.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada. Canada has no general foreign-exchange administration imposing capital controls or mandatory export-proceeds surrender. The Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) administers federal anti-money-laundering and anti-terrorist-financing requirements for reporting entities, while the Canada Border Services Agency and the Canada Revenue Agency administer customs, tax, and certain cross-border reporting obligations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar is freely convertible for ordinary current-account and capital-account transactions. Canada generally permits unrestricted receipt, retention, conversion, and remittance of export proceeds, dividends, interest, royalties, shareholder-loan repayments, and capital. A Canadian ULC must satisfy corporate-law solvency requirements, contractual restrictions, withholding-tax obligations, transfer-pricing requirements, beneficial-ownership verification, sanctions screening, and bank transaction-monitoring controls before remitting funds. Dividends and other payments to non-residents may be subject to Canadian withholding tax unless reduced or eliminated under an applicable tax treaty. Related-party financing must be commercially supportable and documented. Cross-border transactions may require tax filings, information reporting, customs records, and records supporting the stated economic purpose.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Canada has no statutory export-proceeds surrender requirement, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no general statutory deadline requiring conversion of foreign-currency export receipts into Canadian dollars. Export proceeds may be retained in foreign-currency accounts or converted at the company's discretion. The company should retain contracts, invoices, shipping records, customs documentation, payment confirmations, and foreign-exchange records. Banks may impose internal settlement, documentation, sanctions, or anti-money-laundering requirements. Electronic funds transfers of CAD 10,000 or more, or aggregated transfers meeting applicable reporting thresholds, may trigger FINTRAC reporting by the financial institution; this is a reporting obligation and not a surrender rule.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium to High for payment collection, foreign-currency conversion, and outbound transfers, subject to provider jurisdiction and product scope. Canada does not operate a single European-style electronic-money-institution licensing regime. A foreign digital EMI or payment provider may be unable to provide unrestricted Canadian payment services without complying with applicable Canadian requirements, including registration under the Retail Payment Activities Act where it performs in-scope retail payment activities, FINTRAC registration as a money services business where applicable, sanctions compliance, client-money safeguarding, privacy obligations, and provincial consumer or securities requirements. An offshore EMI should not be treated as a substitute for a Canadian deposit-taking account, and CAD account availability, Canadian clearing access, insolvency protection, settlement timing, and account termination risk must be contractually assessed.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical attendance by directors is not universally required in Canada. Major banks commonly permit remote onboarding where identity, authority, beneficial ownership, source of funds, and business purpose can be independently verified. A branch visit, video interview, notarized or certified documents, or enhanced due diligence may be required based on ownership complexity, foreign directors, ULC structure, high-risk jurisdictions, unusual payment flows, or inability to verify the principal place of business. The bank may require Canadian-resident signing officers, an operating address, Canadian tax information, and evidence of an active Canadian business.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unlimited-liability corporate form viewed as unusual, tax-sensitive, or inconsistent with the stated operating model
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate and articles of incorporation; Alberta corporate registry profile; shareholder and director registers; beneficial-ownership information; written explanation of the ULC structure; organizational chart; tax classification memorandum; board resolutions; business plan; and confirmation that the entity is used for genuine plush-toy manufacturing and trading activity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Foreign ownership, foreign directors, or complex ownership chain
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified constitutional documents for each relevant entity; complete ownership chart to the ultimate natural-person owners; passports and residential-address evidence; corporate registry extracts; director and officer details; tax-residency certificates where relevant; shareholder agreements; and notarized or apostilled documents if requested by the bank.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear source of initial capital or shareholder loans
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed subscription or loan agreements; board and shareholder resolutions; bank statements; audited or management financial statements; tax returns or tax assessments; sale-of-business or investment records; proof of accumulated earnings; and a funds-flow schedule matching the remitting account to the beneficial owner.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Expected cross-border payments involving multiple currencies, offshore platforms, or payment intermediaries
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Treasury policy; payment-flow diagram; counterparties list; customer and supplier contracts; invoices; purchase orders; shipping and customs documents; platform agreements; expected monthly volume and transaction-size profile; foreign-exchange policy; sanctions-screening procedure; and explanation of each payment intermediary's regulatory status.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High cash intensity or transactions inconsistent with a low-risk plush-toy OEM profile
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Sales-channel analysis; customer concentration report; payment-method policy; cash-handling controls; inventory and production records; invoices and receipts; anti-fraud controls; reconciliation procedures; and management certification that cash receipts are incidental and commercially justified.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payments involving sanctioned, embargoed, or high-risk jurisdictions or counterparties
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Counterparty due-diligence files; sanctions-screening results; beneficial-owner confirmations; end-use and end-user statements; shipping route; customs classification; certificates of origin; export-control analysis; and documented escalation and approval records.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch between declared business activity and account activity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Industry description aligned to computerized embroidery, ultrasonic seaming, and custom plush-doll OEM production; production contracts; supplier and customer master files; factory or warehouse lease; equipment invoices; payroll records; inventory reports; projected financial statements; and monthly bank-reconciliation controls.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Incomplete corporate authority or inability to identify authorized signers
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current corporate registry documents; director resolutions; banking resolution; signing mandate; specimen signatures; powers of attorney; identification for all authorized persons; and evidence that account permissions follow segregation-of-duties controls.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route equity contributions and shareholder loans from an account held in the name of the documented investor or lender through a regulated bank using a transparent wire description such as equity contribution, share subscription, or shareholder loan. Canada does not prescribe a universal central-bank purpose-code system for these transfers; the sending and receiving banks may require their own payment-purpose classification. Maintain the subscription agreement or loan agreement, board and shareholder approvals, capitalization table, source-of-funds evidence, beneficial-owner information, and remittance confirmation. Avoid third-party funding unless fully documented. Reconcile the incoming wire to the general ledger and corporate records. For shareholder loans, document principal, maturity, interest, currency, repayment terms, transfer-pricing support, and any Canadian withholding-tax implications. Banks may require enhanced review for large or unusual capital injections, and FINTRAC reporting may apply to the financial institution.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use Canadian bank wires, correspondent-bank transfers, electronic funds transfers, or approved payment-platform rails for supplier and customer settlements. SWIFT MT103 remains a commonly understood customer-credit-transfer reference, but ISO 20022 payment messages are increasingly used and may replace legacy formats in relevant corridors. For documentary trade, use a commercial letter of credit subject to UCP 600, with document examination, discrepancy controls, sanctions screening, and shipping-document verification. For open-account purchases, require approved purchase orders, commercial invoices, shipping evidence, customs records, beneficiary verification, and three-way matching against goods received. Reconcile settlement currency, value date, bank fees, foreign-exchange rate, and realized gain or loss. Canadian-dollar domestic settlement may use Payments Canada rails, including wire services or other eligible bank payment systems; availability depends on the financial institution and transaction type.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable foreign-exchange forwards with an appropriately regulated bank or qualified dealer, supported by documented commercial exposure, approved limits, confirmation procedures, and counterparty credit controls

Non-deliverable forwards for currencies or corridors where physical delivery is restricted or commercially impractical, subject to counterparty eligibility, applicable derivatives rules, reporting requirements, and documented underlying exposure

Currency swaps and cross-currency swaps for funding or liquidity management, documented under an ISDA Master Agreement or equivalent institutional documentation with collateral, valuation, close-out, and netting provisions where appropriate
Foreign-exchange options or collars for permitted risk-management purposes, subject to suitability, disclosure, accounting, counterparty, and derivatives-governance requirements
Spot foreign-exchange transactions for ordinary settlement and working-capital conversion; speculative trading unrelated to a documented business exposure should be prohibited by treasury policy

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: File annually during the corporation's anniversary month, subject to the registry's recorded anniversary date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing may result in registry notices, late charges, and administrative dissolution or strike-off after continued non-filing. The exact enforcement timeline is determined by the Alberta Corporate Registry.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: File within six months after the end of each taxation year. Any corporate income tax balance is generally payable two months after year-end, or three months for qualifying Canadian-controlled private corporations.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalties generally apply where tax is owing, with additional arrears interest and instalment-interest exposure. Persistent non-filing may trigger compliance enforcement, assessments, collection action, and director-liability issues where legally applicable.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No general revenue, asset, or employee threshold automatically requires an audit for a closely held Alberta corporation. An auditor is generally required unless all shareholders validly resolve annually to dispense with the audit and the corporation is not subject to a mandatory audit requirement under its articles, financing documents, securities status, or another statute.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Canadian Generally Accepted Accounting Principles. A private corporation generally uses Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises, while a publicly accountable entity must use IFRS. The selected framework must be applied consistently in the financial statements and tax records.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The corporation must maintain an up-to-date register of individuals with significant control and review the information at least annually. Shareholding, control, and ownership changes must be documented promptly, with supporting identification and ownership records. The register is generally retained at the registered office and is not filed annually with the Alberta Corporate Registry unless a specific filing or authority request applies.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Individuals with Significant Control

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: Approximately USD 300-900 per year, depending on service scope, mail handling, nominee services, and compliance support.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Approximately USD 3,500-12,000 for a small private corporation requiring an independent audit; nil for a validly exempt corporation, although compilation or review services may still be commercially advisable.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: SR&ED tax credits (up to 35% refundable), scientific research and experimental development deductions, no specific tax holidays for plush toy manufacturing

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return filed electronically through My Business Account
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: 6 months after the end of the taxation year

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of $50 per day, maximum $5,000; interest on late payments at prescribed rates

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% federal withholding tax on dividends to non-residents, subject to tax treaty reductions
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Submit Form NR301 to Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) along with tax residency certificate and beneficial ownership declaration to claim reduced treaty rates
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 10% federal statutory rate, reduced by treaties; Interest: 25% federal statutory rate, reduced by treaties (e.g., 0% under some treaties)

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: CAD 500,000 for local file requirements; master file for larger groups
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada applies transfer pricing rules under ITA s. 247; economic substance considerations apply in transfer pricing adjustments and for certain entities under the Income Tax Act

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate understatement of income or false statements in tax return
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal conviction with fines up to $1 million and imprisonment up to 5 years; civil penalties
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face personal liability for willful evasion, including fines, imprisonment, and disqualification from office

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to Maintain Transfer Pricing Documentation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Not preparing or retaining local file or master file as required
